questions.q: A rectangular coil comprising $100$ turns has a length of $5 \text{ cm}$ and a width of $4 \text{ cm}$. It is positioned such that its plane is parallel to a uniform magnetic field, and a current of $2 \text{ A}$ is passed through the coil. Determine the magnitude of the magnetic field $B$ if the torque acting on the coil is $0.2 \text{ N m}^{-1}$.
questions.solution:
The torque acting on a current-carrying coil in a uniform magnetic field is given by:

$\tau = N I A B \sin\theta$

Given that the plane of the coil is parallel to the magnetic field, the angle between the area vector and the magnetic field is $\theta = 90^{}^{{}^{\circ}}$.

Substituting the given values:

$N = 100$

$I = 2 \text{ A}$

$A = 5 \text{ cm} \times 4 \text{ cm} = 20 \text{ cm}^2 = 20 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2$

$\tau = 0.2 \text{ N m}$

We get:

$0.2 = 100 \times 2 \times 20 \times 10^{-4} \times B \times \sin(90^{}^{{}^{\circ}})$

$0.2 = 4000 \times 10^{-4} \times B$

$0.2 = 0.4 \times B$

$B = \dfrac{0.2}{0.4} = 0.5 \text{ T}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A circular coil with $50$ turns and a radius of $2.0 \text{ cm}$ carries a $5.0 \text{ A}$ current while rotating in a magnetic field of strength $0.20 \text{ T}$. Determine the maximum torque exerted on the coil.
questions.solution:
The maximum torque on a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field is given by the formula:

$\tau_{\text\max} = NIAB$

where:
$N$ is the number of turns $= 50$
$I$ is the current $= 5.0 \text{ A}$
$A$ is the area of the coil $= \pi r^2 = \pi (2.0 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m})^2 = 4\pi \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2$
$B$ is the magnetic field $= 0.20 \text{ T}$

Substituting the given values:

$\tau_{\text\max} = 50 \times 5.0 \times (4\pi \times 10^{-4}) \times 0.20$

$\tau_{\text\max} = 250 \times 0.20 \times 4\pi \times 10^{-4}$

$\tau_{\text\max} = 50 \times 4\pi \times 10^{-4}$

$\tau_{\text\max} = 200\pi \times 10^{-4}$

$\tau_{\text\max} = 2\pi \times 10^{-2} \approx 2 \times 3.14 \times 10^{-2} = 6.28 \times 10^{-2} \text{ N m}$

Rounding to two significant figures, we get $6.3 \times 10^{-2} \text{ N m}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A circular coil with $50$ turns and a radius of $2.0 \text{ cm}$ carries a $5.0 \text{ A}$ current while rotating in a magnetic field of strength $0.20 \text{ T}$. At a specific orientation, the torque exerted on the coil is half of its maximum possible value. Determine the angle between the plane of the coil and the magnetic field.
questions.solution:
The torque acting on a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field is given by $\tau = N I A B \sin \theta$

where $\theta$ is the angle between the area vector (normal to the plane of the coil) and the magnetic field.

The maximum torque is $\tau_{\text\max} = N I A B$

Given that the torque is half of its maximum possible value:

$\tau = \dfrac{1}{2} \tau_{\text\max}$

$N I A B \sin \theta = \dfrac{1}{2} N I A B$

$\sin \theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\theta = 30^{}^{{}^{\circ}}$

The angle between the plane of the coil and the magnetic field is $\alpha = 90^{}^{{}^{\circ}} - \theta$

$\alpha = 90^{}^{{}^{\circ}} - 30^{}^{{}^{\circ}} = 60^{}^{{}^{\circ}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A rectangular loop with sides of $20 \text{ cm}$ and $10 \text{ cm}$ carries a current of $5.0 \text{ A}$. A uniform magnetic field of magnitude $0.20 \text{ T}$ is present, directed parallel to the longer side of the loop. Determine the net force acting on the loop.
questions.solution:
The net magnetic force on any closed current-carrying loop placed in a uniform magnetic field is always zero.

The net force is given by $\vec{F}_{net} = \oint I(d\vec{l} \times \vec{B})$.

Since the magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is uniform, it can be taken out of the integral:

$\vec{F}_{net} = I(\oint d\vec{l}) \times \vec{B}$

For any closed loop, the vector sum of all length elements is zero, i.e., $\oint d\vec{l} = 0$.

Therefore, $\vec{F}_{net} = 0$.

Alternatively, the forces on the two longer sides are zero as they are parallel to the magnetic field. The forces on the two shorter sides are equal in magnitude but opposite in direction, cancelling each other out. Thus, the net force is zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A rectangular loop with sides of $20 \text{ cm}$ and $10 \text{ cm}$ carries a current of $5.0 \text{ A}$. A uniform magnetic field of magnitude $0.20 \text{ T}$ is present, directed parallel to the longer side of the loop. Determine the torque acting on the loop.
options: $0.04 \text{ N m}$ parallel to the shorter side
$0.02 \text{ N m}$ parallel to the longer side
$0.04 \text{ N m}$ parallel to the longer side
$0.02 \text{ N m}$ parallel to the shorter side
questions.solution:
Area of the rectangular loop, $A = 20 \text{ cm} \times 10 \text{ cm} = 0.2 \text{ m} \times 0.1 \text{ m} = 0.02 \text{ m}^2$

Magnetic dipole moment of the loop, $M = I A = 5.0 \times 0.02 = 0.1 \text{ A m}^2$

The magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is parallel to the longer side, meaning it lies in the plane of the loop. The magnetic moment $\vec{M}$ is perpendicular to the plane of the loop. Therefore, the angle between $\vec{M}$ and $\vec{B}$ is $90^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$.

Magnitude of torque, $\tau = M B \sin(90^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}) = 0.1 \times 0.20 \times 1 = 0.02 \text{ N m}$

The direction of torque is given by $\vec{\tau} = \vec{M} \times \vec{B}$. Since $\vec{M}$ is perpendicular to the loop's plane and $\vec{B}$ is parallel to the longer side, their cross product is perpendicular to both. This makes the torque vector lie in the plane of the loop and parallel to the shorter side.

questions.q: A circular coil with a radius of $2.0 \text{ cm}$ consists of $500$ turns and carries a current of $1.0 \text{ A}$. The axis of the coil forms an angle of $30^{}^{{}^{\circ}}$ with a uniform magnetic field of magnitude $0.40 \text{ T}$ present in the region. Determine the torque acting on the coil.
questions.solution:
Given:
Radius of the coil, $r = 2.0 \text{ cm} = 0.02 \text{ m}$
Number of turns, $N = 500$
Current, $I = 1.0 \text{ A}$
Magnetic field, $B = 0.40 \text{ T}$
Angle between the axis of the coil and the magnetic field, $\theta = 30^{}^{{}^{\circ}}$

The magnetic moment of the coil is given by:
$M = N I A = N I (\pi r^2)$

Substituting the values:
$M = 500 \times 1.0 \times \pi \times (0.02)^2 = 500 \times 0.0004 \pi = 0.2 \pi \text{ A m}^2$

The torque acting on the coil is:
$\tau = M B \sin\theta$

Substituting the values:
$\tau = 0.2 \pi \times 0.40 \times \sin 30^{}^{{}^{\circ}}$
$\tau = 0.08 \pi \times 0.5$
$\tau = 0.04 \pi \text{ N m}$

Using $\pi \approx 3.14$:
$\tau \approx 0.04 \times 3.14 = 0.1256 \text{ N m} \approx 0.13 \text{ N m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A circular loop carrying a current $i$ is made of wire with a total length $L$. A uniform magnetic field $B$ is present parallel to the plane of the loop. Determine the torque on the loop.
questions.solution:
Let the radius of the circular loop be $r$.

The total length of the wire is $L$, so $2\pi r = L \Rightarrow r = \dfrac{L}{2\pi}$

The area of the circular loop is $A = \pi r^2 = \pi \left(\dfrac{L}{2\pi}\right)^2 = \dfrac{L^2}{4\pi}$

The magnetic dipole moment of the loop is $M = iA = \dfrac{i L^2}{4\pi}$

Since the magnetic field $B$ is parallel to the plane of the loop, the angle between the magnetic moment vector (which is perpendicular to the plane) and the magnetic field is $\theta = 90^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$

The torque acting on the loop is $\tau = M B \sin \theta$

$\tau = \left(\dfrac{i L^2}{4\pi}\right) B \sin 90^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} = \dfrac{i L^2 B}{4\pi}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wire with a total length $L$ is used to form a square loop carrying a current $i$. A uniform magnetic field $B$ is present parallel to the plane of the loop. Determine the torque on the square loop.
questions.solution:
Let the side length of the square loop be $a$.

Since the total length of the wire is $L$, the perimeter of the square is $4a = L \Rightarrow a = \dfrac{L}{4}$.

The area of the square loop is $A = a^2 = \left(\dfrac{L}{4}\right)^2 = \dfrac{L^2}{16}$.

The magnetic dipole moment of the loop is $M = iA = \dfrac{iL^2}{16}$.

The magnetic field $B$ is parallel to the plane of the loop, so the angle between the area vector of the loop and the magnetic field is $\theta = 90^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$.

The magnitude of the torque on the loop is $\tau = MB\sin\theta$.

Substituting the values, we get $\tau = \left(\dfrac{iL^2}{16}\right)B\sin 90^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} = \dfrac{iL^2B}{16}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A square coil with $n$ turns and an edge length $l$ carries a current $i$. It is placed on a smooth horizontal plate. A uniform magnetic field $B$ is present in a direction parallel to one of its edges. The total mass of the coil is $M$. Determine the minimum value of $B$ required for the coil to start tipping over.
questions.solution:
The magnetic moment of the square coil is given by $\mu = n i A = n i l^2$.

Since the magnetic field $B$ is parallel to one of the edges of the coil, it lies in the plane of the coil. The angle between the magnetic moment vector $\vec{\mu}$ (which is perpendicular to the plane of the coil) and the magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is $90^{\circ}$.

The torque exerted by the magnetic field on the coil is $\tau_{B} = \mu B \sin 90^{\circ} = n i l^2 B$.

This magnetic torque tends to lift one edge of the coil and tip it over the opposite edge. The restoring torque is provided by the weight of the coil.

The weight $M g$ acts through the center of mass of the square coil, which is at a perpendicular distance of $\dfrac{l}{2}$ from any edge.

The restoring torque about the tipping edge is $\tau_{g} = M g $\$left(\dfrac{l}{2}\right).

For the coil to just start tipping over, the magnetic torque must be equal to or greater than the restoring torque:

$\tau_{B} \ge \tau_{g}$

$n i l^2 B \ge $\dfrac{M g l}{2}

$B \ge $\dfrac{M g}{2 n i l}

Thus, the minimum value of the magnetic field required is \dfrac{M g}{2 n i l}.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A nonconducting ring of radius $r$ and mass $m$ carries a total charge $q$ that is uniformly distributed over it. The ring is rotated about its axis with an angular speed $\omega$. Determine the equivalent electric current in the ring.
questions.solution:
The total charge on the ring is $q$.

The ring rotates with an angular speed $\omega$.

The time period of one complete rotation is $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$.

The equivalent electric current $I$ is the total charge passing a given point per unit time.

$I = \dfrac{q}{T}$

$I = \dfrac{q}{\dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}} = \dfrac{q \omega}{2\pi}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A nonconducting ring of radius $r$ and mass $m$ carries a total charge $q$ that is uniformly distributed over it. The ring is rotated about its axis with an angular speed $\omega$. Determine the magnetic moment $\mu$ of the ring.
questions.solution:
The rotating charge on the ring constitutes an equivalent electric current.

The equivalent current is given by $i = \dfrac{q}{T}$, where $T$ is the time period of rotation.

Since the angular speed is $\omega$, the time period is $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$.

Therefore, the current is $i = \dfrac{q \omega}{2\pi}$.

The magnetic moment $\mu$ of a current loop is the product of the current and the area of the loop.

The area of the ring is $A = \pi r^2$.

Substituting the values, we get $\mu = i A = \left(\dfrac{q \omega}{2\pi}\right) (\pi r^2) = \dfrac{q \omega r^2}{2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A nonconducting ring of radius $r$ and mass $m$ carries a total charge $q$ that is uniformly distributed over it. The ring is rotated about its axis with an angular speed $\omega$. If $l$ represents the angular momentum of the ring about its axis of rotation, which of the following gives the correct relation between its magnetic moment $\mu$ and $l$?
questions.solution:
The equivalent current due to the rotating charge is given by $I = \dfrac{q}{T} = \dfrac{q \omega}{2\pi}$.

The magnetic moment of the ring is $\mu = I A = \left(\dfrac{q \omega}{2\pi}\right) (\pi r^2) = \dfrac{1}{2} q \omega r^2$.

The angular momentum of the ring about its axis of rotation is $l = m r^2 \omega$.

Taking the ratio of magnetic moment to angular momentum, we get:

$\dfrac{\mu}{l} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2} q \omega r^2}{m r^2 \omega} = \dfrac{q}{2m}$

Therefore, $\mu = \dfrac{q}{2m} l$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A nonconducting plate of mass $m$ and radius $r$ has a charge $q$ uniformly distributed over it. The plate rotates about its axis with an angular speed $\omega$. What is the relationship between the magnetic moment $\mu$ and the angular momentum $l$ of the plate?
questions.solution:
For a uniform distribution of charge and mass, the ratio of magnetic moment $\mu$ to angular momentum $l$ can be found by considering an elemental ring of radius $x$ and thickness $dx$ on the plate.

The charge on this ring is $dq = \dfrac{q}{\pi r^2} (2\pi x dx) = \dfrac{2q}{r^2} x dx$

The equivalent current due to the rotation of this ring is $di = \dfrac{dq}{T} = \dfrac{dq \omega}{2\pi} = \dfrac{q \omega}{\pi r^2} x dx$

The magnetic moment of this elemental ring is $d\mu = di (\pi x^2) = \dfrac{q \omega}{r^2} x^3 dx$

Integrating from $x = 0$ to $x = r$, the total magnetic moment is:

$\mu = \int_{0}^{r} \dfrac{q \omega}{r^2} x^3 dx = \dfrac{q \omega r^2}{4}$

The angular momentum of the circular plate (disk) about its axis is:

$l = I\omega = \dfrac{mr^2}{2} \omega$

Taking the ratio of magnetic moment to angular momentum:

$\dfrac{\mu}{l} = \dfrac{\dfrac{q \omega r^2}{4}}{\dfrac{m r^2 \omega}{2}} = \dfrac{q}{2m}$

$\mu = \dfrac{q}{2m} l$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Consider a solid sphere of radius $r$ and mass $m$ having a charge $q$ distributed uniformly throughout its volume. The sphere rotates about a diameter with an angular speed $\omega$. The relationship between the magnetic moment $\mu$ and the angular momentum $l$ of the sphere is given by
questions.solution:
For a rigid body having uniform charge and mass distribution, the ratio of charge to mass for any elemental volume is constant.

Let the uniform charge density be $\rho_q = \dfrac{q}{V}$ and uniform mass density be $\rho_m = \dfrac{m}{V}$.

Consider an elemental volume $dV$ rotating at a perpendicular distance $x$ from the axis of rotation with angular speed $\omega$.

The charge of the element is $dq = \rho_q dV$ and its mass is $dm = \rho_m dV$.

The magnetic moment of this rotating element is $d\mu = \dfrac{1}{2} dq x^2 \omega$.

The angular momentum of the element is $dl = dm x^2 \omega$.

Taking the ratio of the two quantities:

$\dfrac{d\mu}{dl} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2} dq x^2 \omega}{dm x^2 \omega} = \dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{dq}{dm} = \dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{\rho_q dV}{\rho_m dV} = \dfrac{q}{2m}$

Since this ratio is constant for all elements, integrating over the entire volume of the sphere yields:

$\mu = \dfrac{q}{2m} l$
